_comment: Every variable the website reads. `name` must match .env.example (checked), unless `notInExample` gives the reason it is deliberately absent. readBy: Node.

precedence.intro: The settings are read in this order. The first one that has a value wins.

steps.title: The real environment
steps.text: A variable set in the terminal (export NAME=value) or by the host. It always wins over the file, so a deployment can override .env without editing it.

steps.title: The env file
steps.text: The file named by TERUCON_ENV_FILE, otherwise .env next to package.json. It is re-read whenever it changes: save it and reload the page. Only HOST and PORT need a restart.

steps.title: The built-in default
steps.text: What the column below shows. A blank value in the file counts as not set.

precedence.envFileNote: The way to point the website at a different file (a relative path is relative to the project folder). Every test sets it, together with an explicit environment, so no test can ever read your real .env.

groups.title: Where the website listens
groups.blurb: Read by Express. HOST and PORT need a restart.

groups.title: The Design Studio's cold start
groups.blurb: Read by Express. Takes effect on the next request (no restart).

groups.title: Keeping the open studio safe
groups.blurb: Read by Express. STUDIO_REQUIRE_PASSCODE and TRUST_PROXY need a restart; the limits take effect on the next request.

groups.title: Analytics (PostHog)
groups.blurb: Read by Express and asked for by every page (GET /api/analytics). Takes effect on the next request.

vars.name: HOST
vars.effect: Where Express listens. 127.0.0.1 means only this computer. 0.0.0.0 exposes the server to the network: use it only on a trusted network.

vars.name: PORT
vars.effect: The port Express listens on. If it is taken, the server says so and exits.

vars.name: ALLOWED_HOSTS
vars.effect: Extra host names the site may be opened under (comma separated), for when it is served from a domain. Any other Host header is refused with 421.

vars.name: TERUCON_ENV_FILE
vars.effect: Path of the env file. Relative paths are relative to the project folder. Tests always set it.
vars.notInExample: it chooses the file, so it cannot live inside it; set it in the real environment

vars.name: STUDIO_WARMUP
vars.effect: The Design Studio's GPU services scale to zero and take 10-45 s to wake. With on, the landing page and the studio page ask the website to start them as soon as they open (POST /api/studio/warmup), so they are usually ready by the first scan; a started service is billed until it has been idle for a few minutes, even if the visitor never uploads a photo. With off the studio wakes them only when a photo is scanned.

vars.name: STUDIO_REQUIRE_PASSCODE
vars.effect: off: the website switches the studio's own STUDIO_PASSCODE (swatchroom/.env) off before the studio reads its settings, and puts server/lib/studioShield.js in front of it. on: the studio asks for its passcode as it does on its own, and the shield is not used. Read when the server starts.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_AI
vars.effect: Gemini calls (/api/ai) one browser may start per hour.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_VISION
vars.effect: Photo scans (/api/vision) one browser may start per hour.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_PIPELINE
vars.effect: Room analyses and wake-ups (/api/pipeline) one browser may start per hour.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_CHECK
vars.effect: Settings > Check runs (/api/check) one browser may start per hour.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_ROOMS
vars.effect: Room and room-file saves and deletes (/api/rooms) one browser may do per hour. Autosave is frequent, so this is the highest.

vars.name: STUDIO_LIMIT_ADDRESS_FACTOR
vars.effect: One network address may do this many times a browser's limit (a shared address: an office, a phone network), which also stops a visitor who clears cookies to get a new allowance.

vars.name: TRUST_PROXY
vars.effect: How many proxies sit in front of the site (Render: 1, set in render.yaml), or the proxy addresses. Without it the site sees the proxy's address for every visitor and cannot tell HTTPS from HTTP. Read when the server starts.

vars.name: POSTHOG_KEY
vars.effect: PostHog project key (phc_...), public by PostHog's design. Blank: the studio's own key in swatchroom/.env is used. Neither set: no analytics.

vars.name: POSTHOG_HOST
vars.effect: The API host PostHog gave the project; must be https. A malformed host switches analytics off.

vars.name: POSTHOG_REPLAY
vars.effect: Session replay, with all text and fields masked and photos blocked. It also needs replay switched on in the PostHog project itself.

vars.name: POSTHOG_ON_LOCALHOST
vars.effect: Off: nothing is sent while the site is opened as localhost, so test clicks do not fill the real project. on: send from this computer too.
